title.value: Rethinking Generalization: The Impact of Annotation Style on Medical Image Segmentation
title.justification: The paper's primary focus is on the impact of annotation styles on medical image segmentation, as suggested by the title.
title.quote: Rethinking Generalization: The Impact of Annotation Style on Medical Image Segmentation

extractions.description: This paper explores how different annotation styles can impact the generalization of deep learning models in medical image segmentation. It proposes a method to model these differences in annotation styles using Conditioned Instance Normalization (CIN), allowing for the accommodation and identification of annotation biases across multiple medical datasets. The study emphasizes the importance of accounting for annotation style in evaluating model performance and combines this with a systematic approach to identifying similar annotation styles for effective data pooling and model fine-tuning.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper discusses medical image segmentation and mentions biases, this does not directly connect to themes of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This is particularly important in the context of medical image segmentation of pathological structures (e.g. lesions), where the annotation process is much more subjective, and affected by a number underlying factors, including the annotation protocol, rater education/experience, and clinical aims, among others.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on medical image segmentation, model biases, and generalization, which do not directly pertain to any area of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: In this paper, we show that modeling annotation biases, rather than ignoring them, poses a promising way of accounting for differences in annotation style across datasets.

secondary_categories.justification: The secondary topics still focus on medical data and generalization rather than ecological topics.
secondary_categories.quote: To illustrate how annotation biases arise in practice, consider an example where Hospital A is measuring lesion counts in multiple sclerosis (MS) patients, and where Hospital B is measuring lesion volumes in MS patients.

primary_sub_category.justification: The study and its applications are centered on improving medical image analytics rather than environmental or ecological topics.
primary_sub_category.quote: The relationship between these sets of trials is also demonstrated in the quantitative results presented in Table 2.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Again, secondary focus on methods related to medical datasets does not translate to ecological sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: To validate the conclusions obtained from this method, another series of experiments using the identified groups are conducted in this section.

applications.value: Medical image segmentation for multiple sclerosis
applications.justification: The application focuses on improving segmentation outcomes by accounting for annotation style biases when analyzing MRI images in medical context.
applications.quote: We evaluate our approach using six different MS clinical trial datasets and provide an in-depth analysis of the challenges that different annotation styles can present to supervised medical image segmentation approaches.

new_primary_category.justification: The current focus and applications do not warrant a new sustainable development category as they remain outside climate or ecological contexts.
new_primary_category.quote: Supervised deep learning medical image segmentation models rely heavily on annotations.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category needs defining since the paper is outside the realm of climate or ecological subcategories.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: In addition to human factors, the label generation process itself can be a major contributor to annotation style.
